30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely

30:21.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا لِّتَسۡكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
30:21.en: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect

30:22.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ خَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفُ أَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَأَلۡوَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡعَٰلِمِينَ
30:22.en: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge

30:23.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ مَنَامُكُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱبۡتِغَآؤُكُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَسۡمَعُونَ
30:23.en: And of His signs is your slumber by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who heed

30:24.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلۡبَرۡقَ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَيُحۡيِۦ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:24.en: And of His signs is this: He showeth you the lightning for a fear and for a hope, and sendeth down water from the sky, and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who understand

30:25.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۚ ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ دَعۡوَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِذَآ أَنتُمۡ تَخۡرُجُونَ
30:25.en: And of His signs is this: The heavens and the earth stand fast by His command, and afterward, when He calleth you, lo! from the earth ye will emerge

31:31.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُم مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
31:31.en: Hast thou not seen how the ships glide on the sea by Allah's grace, that He may show you of His wonders? Lo! therein indeed are portents for every steadfast, grateful (heart)

31:32.ar: وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُم مَّوۡجࣱ كَٱلظُّلَلِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ فَمِنۡهُم مُّقۡتَصِدࣱۚ وَمَا يَجۡحَدُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارࣲ كَفُورࣲ‏
31:32.en: And if a wave enshroudeth them like awnings, they cry unto Allah, making their faith pure for Him only. But when He bringeth them safe to land, some of them compromise. None denieth Our signs save every traitor ingrate

32:26.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لَهُمۡ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ يَمۡشُونَ فِي مَسَٰكِنِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٍۚ أَفَلَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
32:26.en: Is it not a guidance for them (to observe) how many generations We destroyed before them, amid whose dwelling places they do walk? Lo! therein verily are portents! Will they not then heed

32:27.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلۡمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡجُرُزِ فَنُخۡرِجُ بِهِۦ زَرۡعࣰ ا تَأۡكُلُ مِنۡهُ أَنۡعَٰمُهُمۡ وَأَنفُسُهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
32:27.en: Have they not seen how We lead the water to the barren land and therewith bring forth crops whereof their cattle eat, and they themselves? Will they not then see

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

B7gEy-jOdls.speaker: adnan
B7gEy-jOdls.speaker_note: single speaker in the sheikh's Ramadan nightly Quranic Themes series; speaks of his students and his family's village
B7gEy-jOdls.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 20: Divine Signs
B7gEy-jOdls.one_line: Build iman on the constant signs of Allah in creation, history and the self, through Ar-Rum, Luqman and As-Sajdah.
B7gEy-jOdls.summary: Divine signs are a major Quranic theme and the first thing prophets were sent to recite; they are 'recited' because, like written words, they never change. The Quran asks us to contemplate ordinary things everyone sees, not specialist science, and to think past the sign to the One who set it in motion, since people who contemplate without guidance end up worshipping the sun or the stars. His central argument is that iman must rest on constants: the universe, history and one's own inner life. Faith built on answered duas, on circumstances or on a favourite imam collapses when those change; the only person to build on is the Prophet. He then reads the 'and among His signs' verses of Ar-Rum: humans made from soil, spouses for tranquillity, love and mercy, diversity of tongues and colours, night and day, lightning and rain. In Luqman, ships float by His will, and people who call on Him sincerely in a storm grow lukewarm once ashore, lacking patience and gratitude. In As-Sajdah, we walk over the ruins of nations that once ruled, a reminder that we are temporary variables with no grounds for arrogance, while dead earth revived by rain points to Allah. Allah has worked on His side of the relationship; ours is to respond.

outline.heading: Counting the last ten nights
outline.gist: The first and second tens are fixed; the last ten are nine or ten nights depending on whether Ramadan has 29 or 30 days.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reciting His signs: why prophets were sent
outline.gist: The first task of every prophet is to recite Allah's signs, and they are 'recited' because, like the words of a book, they are always there and never change.

outline.heading: Everyday signs, not specialist knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran does not ask for reflection that needs a degree; faith rests on the simple things everyone sees and most people take for granted.

outline.heading: Contemplation without guidance ends in worshipping the sign
outline.gist: Those who marvelled at the stars, sun or mountains without guidance worshipped them.

outline.heading: Think bigger: the force behind the signs
outline.gist: The Quran tells us to look past each sign to the One who put it in motion; real contemplation of sunrise, seasons and running water steadily strengthens iman.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum's wedding verses and our relationship with His laws
outline.gist: The verses read at weddings everywhere describe our relationship with Allah's laws in creation, and the key to it is contemplation.

outline.heading: Iman built on answered duas collapses
outline.gist: If faith depends on getting what you ask for, it crumbles when Allah delays or answers differently; he has seen individuals and whole populations lose faith this way.

outline.heading: The constants: the universe, history and your own self
outline.gist: Observing creation, reading history and knowing your own psyche give a foundation that does not change until the Day you have prepared for.

outline.heading: Never build iman on a person
outline.gist: Imams fall into scandal and people's faith falls with them; he tells his students to keep him out of their iman and look only to the Prophet.

outline.heading: From mud to thinking, feeling human beings
outline.gist: We came from soil and will return to it; mud cannot speak, yet Allah made from it beings who reason, love and hold morals, and we treat that as a given.

outline.heading: Spouses for tranquillity, love and mercy
outline.gist: Each person is restless until completed by a spouse; the consistent male and female design across species is purposeful, not random.

outline.heading: The Quran speaks to the norm, not the exception
outline.gist: Rare cases in nature or life do not overturn the rule; the Quran addresses the norm and exceptions are handled individually with a scholar.

outline.heading: Diversity of tongues and colours
outline.gist: The creation of the heavens and earth and the variety of languages, races and cultures are signs for those with knowledge.

outline.heading: Night for sleep, day for work
outline.gist: We are built for this cycle, and those who work long night shifts for years pay for it in their health and happiness.

outline.heading: Lightning, rain and the call to rise
outline.gist: Lightning brings fear and hope of rain that revives dead earth, and the heavens and earth stand by His command until He calls us out of the ground.

outline.heading: Ships that float by His will
outline.gist: A floating city of metal is accepted without thought; if the physics changed slightly ships would sink and there would be nothing to do, which is a sign for the patient and grateful.

outline.heading: The sea shaped human history
outline.gist: Sea travel and trade let humanity communicate and develop, and today's wars are still fought over access to sea routes.

outline.heading: Sincere in the storm, lukewarm ashore
outline.gist: When waves rise like mountains people call on Allah with full sincerity; once safe they become merely moderate and pray yawning, hoping the imam finishes early.

outline.heading: No composure, no gratitude
outline.gist: Those who reject the signs lack patience, like a toddler whose world ends over dropped ice cream, and lack gratitude; remember how you were in the storm.

outline.heading: Middle-aged and iman still unsettled?
outline.gist: It troubles him when people reach middle age with weak iman, since the signs have never changed and all point to one Creator.

outline.heading: Allah worked on the relationship; now your side
outline.gist: Like a marriage, every relationship needs effort; Allah created, provided, sent guidance and rescued us repeatedly, so our dua is a response to a conversation He began.

outline.heading: Walking over the dwellings of destroyed nations
outline.gist: Places where prophets preached are now poor markets, and Roman arches near his village, where a king once ruled, sit behind a garbage dump.

outline.heading: We are variables: no room for arrogance
outline.gist: Nothing stays the same and we are here briefly, so we must build on the constants and cannot deny the constant One behind them.

outline.heading: Dead earth revived: find Allah by observing
outline.gist: Water driven to barren land brings crops for livestock and people; the cycle of death and life shows that Allah is found by observing His creation, which leads to submission.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Contemplation and deep reflection (tafakkur)
themes.note: The Quran asks for reflection on ordinary everyday signs, looking past each one to the One who made it; unguided contemplation ends in idolatry.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Iman must rest on constants such as creation, history and the self, not on answered duas, circumstances or any person except the Prophet.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Spouses complete each other's restlessness with tranquillity, love and mercy, a purposeful design.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Quranic statements describe the norm; exceptions are dealt with case by case.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: The signs of the sea are for the patient and grateful; people sincere in danger forget Allah once rescued.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Allah has done His part in the relationship; ours is to respond and keep working on it through its dry spells.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: The ruins of once-mighty nations show we are temporary, which leaves no ground for arrogance.

quran.point: Prophets are sent first to recite Allah's signs to their people.

maxims: Build your iman on constants, not variables
You and I are variables
Make sure I have nothing to do with your iman
The Quran speaks to the norm, not the exception
When you make dua, you are responding, not initiating

stories.who: Followers of an imam caught in a scandal
stories.point: Faith resting on a person collapses with that person; only the Prophet is a safe foundation.
Going against the night and day cycle Allah designed takes a toll on body and mood.

stories.who: A toddler whose ice cream falls
stories.point: Losing all composure at the first setback is the opposite of the patience the verse praises.

stories.who: Roman arches by a garbage dump near his family's village
stories.point: A king once ruled there; now nobody cares, a sign that power and people pass.

contemporary: Imams caught in scandals and the effect on followers' faith
Current wars over access to sea routes
takeaways: Set aside time to really contemplate everyday signs: sunrise, night and day, rain, and how human life came from soil.
Base your iman on constants and on the Prophet, not on answered duas or on any scholar or imam.
Hold on to the sincerity you feel in moments of danger after you are safe.
Work on your side of the relationship with Allah; make dua as your reply to His word.
Let the ruins of past nations remind you that you are temporary and keep you from arrogance.

36:54.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
36:54.en: This day no soul is wronged in aught; nor are ye requited aught save what ye used to do

36:55.ar: إِنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ فِي شُغُلࣲ فَٰكِهُونَ
36:55.en: Lo! those who merit paradise this day are happily employed

36:56.ar: هُمۡ وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُمۡ فِي ظِلَٰلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرَآئِكِ مُتَّكِـُٔونَ
36:56.en: They and their wives, in pleasant shade, on thrones reclining

36:57.ar: لَهُمۡ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةࣱ وَلَهُم مَّا يَدَّعُونَ
36:57.en: Theirs the fruit (of their good deeds) and theirs (all) that they ask

36:58.ar: سَلَٰمࣱ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبࣲّ رَّحِيمࣲ‏
36:58.en: The word from a Merciful Lord (for them) is: Peace

36:59.en: But avaunt ye, O ye guilty, this day

36:60.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ أَعۡهَدۡ إِلَيۡكُمۡ يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ أَن لَّا تَعۡبُدُواْ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
36:60.en: Did I not charge you, O ye sons of Adam, that ye worship not the devil - Lo! he is your open foe

36:61.en: But that ye worship Me? That was the right path

36:62.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمۡ جِبِلࣰّ ا كَثِيرًاۖ أَفَلَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡقِلُونَ
36:62.en: Yet he hath led astray of you a great multitude. Had ye then no sense

36:63.en: This is hell which ye were promised (if ye followed him)

36:64.en: Burn therein this day for that ye disbelieved

36:65.ar: ٱلۡيَوۡمَ نَخۡتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَتَشۡهَدُ أَرۡجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
36:65.en: This day We seal up their mouths, and their hands speak out to Us and their feet bear witness as to what they used to earn

36:66.ar: وَلَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَطَمَسۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ فَٱسۡتَبَقُواْ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ فَأَنَّىٰ يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:66.en: And had We willed, We verily could have quenched their eyesight so that they should struggle for the way. Then how could they have seen

36:67.ar: وَلَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَمَسَخۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِهِمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَطَٰعُواْ مُضِيࣰّ ا وَلَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:67.en: And had We willed, We verily could have fixed them in their place, making them powerless to go forward or turn back

15:42.ar: إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيۡسَ لَكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُلۡطَٰنٌ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
15:42.en: Lo! as for My slaves, thou hast no power over any of them save such of the froward as follow thee

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

41:22.ar: وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
41:22.en: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did

41:23.ar: وَذَٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرۡدَىٰكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
41:23.en: That, your thought which ye did think about your Lord, hath ruined you; and ye find yourselves (this day) among the lost

22:46.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ يَعۡقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ ءَاذَانࣱ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
22:46.en: Have they not travelled in the land, and have they hearts wherewith to feel and ears wherewith to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts, which are within the bosoms, that grow blind

GFhmSBeQJA0.speaker: adnan
GFhmSBeQJA0.speaker_note: continues his own Yasin series; speaks of his clinic patients and arriving in London in 2013
GFhmSBeQJA0.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 6 (55-67)
GFhmSBeQJA0.one_line: Paradise as a busy, joyful life, loneliness in this one, Shaytan's sworn hatred of humanity, and limbs that testify on Judgment Day.
GFhmSBeQJA0.summary: He recaps the three barriers to a living heart: failing to reflect, selfish materialism and asking the wrong question. The people of paradise are busy with enjoyment, a word he uses to correct young Muslims who picture paradise as boring. What is removed there is death, disease and sorrow, not stimulation; Allah's creation is vast, and a changed perspective frees people from the petty concerns that consume us here, just as facing death does now. Paradise is shared with spouses, which leads him to the loneliness of the elderly in the West: patients who drive hours just to talk to him, and an elderly couple whose six children all lived far away, compared with village elders who have a mosque, neighbours and someone to argue with. His teacher said the best of paradise is access to Allah's knowledge. Turning to the criminals, Allah asks why anyone ends up there after being warned not to follow Shaytan, a sworn enemy who hates humanity, as do people who share his hatred. The straight path means every step is clean, and Shaytan works by flooding us with options. On that day mouths are sealed and limbs testify, exposing the intentions we hid. He closes with a reading that the final verses mean Allah could have removed our choice, but gave it to us.

outline.heading: The life of the heart as a purpose of the deen
outline.gist: The health of what is inside you is as important as physical health, and is a major theme in the books of spiritual wayfaring.

outline.heading: First barrier: failing to reflect
outline.gist: Not learning from what came before or what lies ahead blocks the heart.

outline.heading: Second barrier: selfish materialism
outline.gist: Told to give, they make an absurd argument driven by greed.

outline.heading: Third barrier: asking the wrong question
outline.gist: Asking when the Hour comes is superficial; someone certain of it prepares instead.

outline.heading: Reading notes: the noon that disappears
outline.gist: He recites the passage and notes where the noon and tanween are fully merged with no trace in the recitation.

outline.heading: No soul wronged, then the outcomes
outline.gist: After the single blast and fair judgment, Allah describes the two outcomes.

outline.heading: The people of paradise are busy with enjoyment
outline.gist: Shughul means being preoccupied, and fakihun links to fruit eaten purely for pleasure; the description is full of life.

outline.heading: Paradise is not boring
outline.gist: Many young Muslims imagine a dull paradise; what is removed is only death, disease and sorrow, not stimulation.

outline.heading: An infinite creation to explore
outline.gist: We are a small, simple part of creation; in paradise people are exposed to far more, having learned gratitude and perseverance here.

outline.heading: Choice makes us stewards
outline.gist: Unlike creatures on a fixed track, humans choose, so we are responsible for others; forgetting this has nearly fried the planet.

outline.heading: The vastness of paradise
outline.gist: Its gates are vast and even the lowest dweller holds many times the size of the earth.

outline.heading: A changed perspective: losing without sorrow
outline.gist: People still strive and may lose, but a heightened understanding removes the overreaction and sorrow.

outline.heading: Death puts things in perspective
outline.gist: Reflecting on death already makes petty quarrels with spouses and siblings fade; Allah will purge such pettiness before paradise.

outline.heading: A different kind of busy, with their spouses
outline.gist: The busyness is not labour, and no one is there alone.

outline.heading: The loneliness of the elderly
outline.gist: Being alone is healthy but loneliness is not; patients drive two hours to his clinic just to talk.

outline.heading: An elderly couple with six children far away
outline.gist: Visiting a lonely immigrant couple after he arrived in 2013 troubled him and his father, unlike village elders surrounded by mosque, family and neighbours.

outline.heading: Shade, couches and whatever they call for
outline.gist: The anxiety of the unknown is gone and every desire is met.

outline.heading: Access to Allah's knowledge
outline.gist: His teacher said the best thing in paradise is unlimited access to divine knowledge, and he shares the excitement of intellectual joy.

outline.heading: Peace, a word from a merciful Lord
outline.gist: No war, oppression, dispute or anyone trying to take what is yours.

outline.heading: Stand apart today, you criminals
outline.gist: Imtiyaz is standing out, and here it is standing out in the wrong direction.

outline.heading: Did I not take a covenant: Shaytan's sworn hatred
outline.gist: Allah pauses to ask why anyone ends up in the fire; Shaytan chose to hate humanity and vowed to prove it unworthy.

outline.heading: Ramadan without jinn devils, but with human ones
outline.gist: Devils among the jinn are chained but human devils keep working, and the jinn are weaker than them.

outline.heading: Those who hate humanity are on Shaytan's page
outline.gist: People who wish destruction, disunity and widening inequality act like Shaytan; we are one family descended from Adam.

outline.heading: Worship Me: a straight path where every step is clean
outline.gist: Linking to his weekday values series, he says the straight path means the means are as pure as the end and people are never means.

outline.heading: He misled mountains of people
outline.gist: Jibill evokes so many people they would stack up like a mountain.

outline.heading: Shaytan's catalogue of options
outline.gist: He has no control over you but floods you with ideas until the right choice is unlikely; learn to tell his whispers from good thoughts.

outline.heading: This is the fire you were promised
outline.gist: Enter it today for your ingratitude.

outline.heading: Mouths sealed, hands and feet testify
outline.gist: Allah lets everything else speak; the person even argues with his own skin.

outline.heading: The self testifies to hidden intentions
outline.gist: A bad assumption about Allah's attention leads to ruin; the corrupt intentions we never admitted will be exposed.

outline.heading: A living heart does not let itself reach that moment
outline.gist: Aware of its intentions now, it makes the right decisions beforehand.

outline.heading: Blinded and frozen in place at the bridge
outline.gist: If Allah willed, their eyes would be covered as they race to cross, or they would be transformed and rooted to the spot.

outline.heading: Another reading: hearts that go blind in this life
outline.gist: One scholar reads the verses as Allah being able to remove our insight to the straight path here; it is hearts, not eyes, that go blind.

outline.heading: We gave you choice
outline.gist: Allah could have made us beings without choice, but gave us the faculties to choose right, and people failed to use them.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Paradise as a busy, stimulating life without death, disease or sorrow, with a transformed perspective.

themes.label: Environment and stewardship of the earth
themes.note: Our ability to choose makes us responsible for creatures that cannot.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Reflecting on death makes petty quarrels fade.

themes.label: Visiting the sick, caring for elders and the vulnerable
themes.note: The loneliness of the elderly in the West compared with village life.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Access to Allah's knowledge as the greatest joy of paradise.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him
themes.note: Shaytan's chosen hatred of humanity, its human counterparts and his method of flooding us with options.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: The straight path means each step is clean; ends do not justify means.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Limbs and the self testify, exposing hidden intentions.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Allah gave us choice instead of fixing us in place, so we bear responsibility for it.

quran.point: Shaytan has no real authority over Allah's servants.
People ask their skins why they testified; Allah made everything speak.
They never guarded against their own limbs and assumed Allah did not know; that assumption ruined them.
It is not the eyes that go blind but the hearts.

hadith.gist: The lowest dweller of paradise will have a dominion many times the size of the earth.
In Ramadan the devils are chained.

stories.point: Six children far away left them isolated; his father said he did not want to die like that.
Mosque, neighbours and family keep the elderly socially alive.

contemporary: Loneliness of elderly immigrants in London, Ontario
Environmental damage caused by humans
His weekday series on Islamic values and moral absolutism
takeaways: Picture paradise as a life of joy and discovery, and correct the idea that it is boring.
Visit and keep company with lonely elders, especially your own parents.
Treat anyone who works to spread hatred and disunity as doing Shaytan's work.
Keep every step clean; do not let ends justify the means.
Be honest with yourself now about your intentions, before your own limbs testify.

25:1.ar: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِۦ لِيَكُونَ لِلۡعَٰلَمِينَ نَذِيرًا
25:1.en: Blessed is He Who hath revealed unto His slave the Criterion (of right and wrong), that he may be a warner to the peoples

25:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكࣱ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقۡدِيرࣰ ا
25:2.en: He unto Whom belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, He hath chosen no son nor hath He any partner in the Sovereignty. He hath created everything and hath meted out for it a measure

25:3.ar: وَٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةࣰ لَّا يَخۡلُقُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُمۡ يُخۡلَقُونَ وَلَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مَوۡتࣰ ا وَلَا حَيَوٰةࣰ وَلَا نُشُورࣰ ا
25:3.en: Yet they choose beside Him other gods who create naught but are themselves created, and possess not hurt nor profit for themselves, and possess not death nor life, nor power to raise the dead

25:4.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ إِفۡكٌ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُ وَأَعَانَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ قَوۡمٌ ءَاخَرُونَۖ فَقَدۡ جَآءُو ظُلۡمࣰ ا وَزُورࣰ ا
25:4.en: Those who disbelieve say: This is naught but a lie that he hath invented, and other folk have helped him with it, so that they have produced a slander and a lie

25:5.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ ٱكۡتَتَبَهَا فَهِيَ تُمۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ بُكۡرَةࣰ وَأَصِيلࣰ ا
25:5.en: And they say: Fables of the men of old which he hath had written down so that they are dictated to him morn and evening

25:6.ar: قُلۡ أَنزَلَهُ ٱلَّذِي يَعۡلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:6.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): He who knoweth the secret of the heavens and the earth hath revealed it. Lo! He ever is Forgiving, Merciful

25:7.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلرَّسُولِ يَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَيَمۡشِي فِي ٱلۡأَسۡوَاقِ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡهِ مَلَكࣱ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُۥ نَذِيرًا
25:7.en: And they say: What aileth this messenger (of Allah) that he eateth food and walketh in the markets? Why is not an angel sent down unto him, to be a warner with him

25:8.ar: أَوۡ يُلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ كَنزٌ أَوۡ تَكُونُ لَهُۥ جَنَّةࣱ يَأۡكُلُ مِنۡهَاۚ وَقَالَ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلࣰ ا مَّسۡحُورًا
25:8.en: Or (why is not) treasure thrown down unto him, or why hath he not a paradise from whence to eat? And the evil-doers say: Ye are but following a man bewitched

25:9.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ ضَرَبُواْ لَكَ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَ فَضَلُّواْ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:9.en: See how they coin similitudes for thee, so that they are all astray and cannot find a road

25:10.ar: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِيٓ إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّن ذَٰلِكَ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكَ قُصُورَۢا
25:10.en: Blessed is He Who, if He will, will assign thee better than (all) that - Gardens underneath which rivers flow - and will assign thee mansions

25:11.ar: بَلۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِٱلسَّاعَةِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِمَن كَذَّبَ بِٱلسَّاعَةِ سَعِيرًا
25:11.en: Nay, but they deny (the coming of) the Hour, and for those who deny (the coming of) the Hour We have prepared a flame

25:12.ar: إِذَا رَأَتۡهُم مِّن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدࣲ سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظࣰ ا وَزَفِيرࣰ ا
25:12.en: When it seeth them from afar, they hear the crackling and the roar thereof

25:13.ar: وَإِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ مِنۡهَا مَكَانࣰ ا ضَيِّقࣰ ا مُّقَرَّنِينَ دَعَوۡاْ هُنَالِكَ ثُبُورࣰ ا
25:13.en: And when they are flung into a narrow place thereof, chained together, they pray for destruction there

25:14.ar: لَّا تَدۡعُواْ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ ثُبُورࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ ا وَٱدۡعُواْ ثُبُورࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:14.en: Pray not that day for one destruction, but pray for many destructions

25:15.ar: قُلۡ أَذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ جَنَّةُ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَۚ كَانَتۡ لَهُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ وَمَصِيرࣰ ا
25:15.en: Say: Is that (doom) better or the Garden of Immortality which is promised unto those who ward off (evil)? It will be their reward and journey's end

25:16.ar: لَّهُمۡ فِيهَا مَا يَشَآءُونَ خَٰلِدِينَۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ وَعۡدࣰ ا مَّسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
25:16.en: Therein abiding, they have all that they desire. It is for thy Lord a promise that must be fulfilled

25:17.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَحۡشُرُهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقُولُ ءَأَنتُمۡ أَضۡلَلۡتُمۡ عِبَادِي هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ أَمۡ هُمۡ ضَلُّواْ ٱلسَّبِيلَ
25:17.en: And on the day when He will assemble them and that which they worship instead of Allah and will say: Was it ye who misled these my slaves or did they (themselves) wander from the way

25:18.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا كَانَ يَنۢبَغِي لَنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِنۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ وَلَٰكِن مَّتَّعۡتَهُمۡ وَءَابَآءَهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ نَسُواْ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمَۢا بُورࣰ ا
25:18.en: They will say: Be Thou Glorified! it was not for us to choose any protecting friends beside thee; but Thou didst give them and their fathers ease till they forgot the warning and became lost folk

25:19.ar: فَقَدۡ كَذَّبُوكُم بِمَا تَقُولُونَ فَمَا تَسۡتَطِيعُونَ صَرۡفࣰ ا وَلَا نَصۡرࣰ اۚ وَمَن يَظۡلِم مِّنكُمۡ نُذِقۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
25:19.en: Thus they will give you the lie regarding what ye say, then ye can neither avert (the doom) nor obtain help. And whoso among you doeth wrong, We shall make him taste great torment

25:20.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا قَبۡلَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ إِلَّآ إِنَّهُمۡ لَيَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَيَمۡشُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَسۡوَاقِۗ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَعۡضَكُمۡ لِبَعۡضࣲ فِتۡنَةً أَتَصۡبِرُونَۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرࣰ ا
25:20.en: We never sent before thee any messengers but lo! they verily ate food and walked in the markets. And We have appointed some of you a test for others: Will ye be steadfast? And thy Lord is ever Seer

25:21.ar: ۞وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَرۡجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَوۡ نَرَىٰ رَبَّنَاۗ لَقَدِ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَعَتَوۡ عُتُوࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
25:21.en: And those who look not for a meeting with Us say: Why are angels not sent down unto us and (Why) do we not see our Lord! Assuredly they think too highly of themselves and are scornful with great pride

25:22.ar: يَوۡمَ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ لَا بُشۡرَىٰ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ لِّلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجۡرࣰ ا مَّحۡجُورࣰ ا
25:22.en: On the day when they behold the angels, on that day there will be no good tidings for the guilty; and they will cry: A forbidding ban

25:23.ar: وَقَدِمۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنۡ عَمَلࣲ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هَبَآءࣰ مَّنثُورًا
25:23.en: And We shall turn unto the work they did and make it scattered motes

25:24.ar: أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَوۡمَئِذٍ خَيۡرࣱ مُّسۡتَقَرࣰّ ا وَأَحۡسَنُ مَقِيلࣰ ا
25:24.en: Those who have earned the Garden on that day will be better in their home and happier in their place of noonday rest

25:25.ar: وَيَوۡمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلۡغَمَٰمِ وَنُزِّلَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ تَنزِيلًا
25:25.en: A day when the heaven with the clouds will be rent asunder and the angels will be sent down, a grand descent

25:26.ar: ٱلۡمُلۡكُ يَوۡمَئِذٍ ٱلۡحَقُّ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِۚ وَكَانَ يَوۡمًا عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَسِيرࣰ ا
25:26.en: The Sovereignty on that day will be the True (Sovereignty) belonging to the Beneficent One, and it will be a hard day for disbelievers

25:27.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:27.en: On the day when the wrong-doer gnaweth his hands, he will say: Ah, would that I had chosen a way together with the messenger (of Allah)

25:28.ar: يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ لَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أَتَّخِذۡ فُلَانًا خَلِيلࣰ ا
25:28.en: Alas for me! Ah, would that I had never taken such an one for friend

25:29.ar: لَّقَدۡ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَنِيۗ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولࣰ ا
25:29.en: He verily led me astray from the Reminder after it had reached me. Satan was ever man's deserter in the hour of need

25:30.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوۡمِي ٱتَّخَذُواْ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ مَهۡجُورࣰ ا
25:30.en: And the messenger saith: O my Lord! Lo! mine own folk make this Qur'an of no account

25:31.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوࣰّ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ هَادِيࣰ ا وَنَصِيرࣰ ا
25:31.en: Even so have We appointed unto every prophet an opponent from among the guilty; but Allah sufficeth for a Guide and Helper

25:32.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ جُمۡلَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَۖ وَرَتَّلۡنَٰهُ تَرۡتِيلࣰ ا
25:32.en: And those who disbelieve say: Why is the Qur'an not revealed unto him all at once? (It is revealed) thus that We may strengthen thy heart therewith; and We have arranged it in right order

25:33.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَحۡسَنَ تَفۡسِيرًا
25:33.en: And they bring thee no similitude but We bring thee the Truth (as against it), and better (than their similitude) as argument

25:34.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحۡشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ شَرࣱّ مَّكَانࣰ ا وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:34.en: Those who will be gathered on their faces unto hell: such are worse in plight and further from the right road

25:35.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلۡنَا مَعَهُۥٓ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ وَزِيرࣰ ا
25:35.en: We verily gave Moses the Scripture and placed with him his brother Aaron as henchman

25:36.ar: فَقُلۡنَا ٱذۡهَبَآ إِلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَدَمَّرۡنَٰهُمۡ تَدۡمِيرࣰ ا
25:36.en: Then We said: Go together unto the folk who have denied Our revelations. Then We destroyed them, a complete destruction

25:37.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُواْ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ لِلنَّاسِ ءَايَةࣰۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
25:37.en: And Noah's folk, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made of them a portent for mankind. We have prepared a painful doom for evil-doers

25:38.ar: وَعَادࣰ ا وَثَمُودَاْ وَأَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُونَۢا بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:38.en: And (the tribes of) A'ad and Thamud, and the dwellers in Ar-Rass, and many generations in between

25:39.ar: وَكُلࣰّ ا ضَرَبۡنَا لَهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَۖ وَكُلࣰّ ا تَبَّرۡنَا تَتۡبِيرࣰ ا
25:39.en: Each (of them) We warned by examples, and each (of them) We brought to utter ruin

25:40.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَتَوۡاْ عَلَى ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أُمۡطِرَتۡ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوۡءِۚ أَفَلَمۡ يَكُونُواْ يَرَوۡنَهَاۚ بَلۡ كَانُواْ لَا يَرۡجُونَ نُشُورࣰ ا
25:40.en: And indeed they have passed by the township whereon was rained the fatal rain. Can it be that they have not seen it? Nay, but they hope for no resurrection

25:41.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَوۡكَ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولًا
25:41.en: And when they see thee (O Muhammad) they treat thee only as a jest (saying): Is this he whom Allah sendeth as a messenger

25:42.ar: إِن كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِنَا لَوۡلَآ أَن صَبَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهَاۚ وَسَوۡفَ يَعۡلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ مَنۡ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
25:42.en: He would have led us far away from our gods if we had not been staunch to them. They will know, when they behold the doom, who is more astray as to the road

25:43.ar: أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيلًا
25:43.en: Hast thou seen him who chooseth for his god his own lust? Wouldst thou then be guardian over him

25:44.ar: أَمۡ تَحۡسَبُ أَنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ يَسۡمَعُونَ أَوۡ يَعۡقِلُونَۚ إِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا كَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ بَلۡ هُمۡ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
25:44.en: Or deemest thou that most of them hear or understand? They are but as the cattle - nay, but they are farther astray

25:45.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنࣰ ا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلࣰ ا
25:45.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread the shade - And if He willed He could have made it still - then We have made the sun its pilot

25:46.ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡنَا قَبۡضࣰ ا يَسِيرࣰ ا
25:46.en: Then We withdraw it unto Us, a gradual withdrawal

25:47.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ لِبَاسࣰ ا وَٱلنَّوۡمَ سُبَاتࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورࣰ ا
25:47.en: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection

25:48.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشۡرَۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ طَهُورࣰ ا
25:48.en: And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy, and We send down purifying water from the sky

25:49.ar: لِّنُحۡـِۧيَ بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ ا وَنُسۡقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقۡنَآ أَنۡعَٰمࣰ ا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:49.en: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof

25:50.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَٰهُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورࣰ ا
25:50.en: And verily We have repeated it among them that they may remember, but most of mankind begrudge aught save ingratitude

25:51.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَبَعَثۡنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرۡيَةࣲ نَّذِيرࣰ ا
25:51.en: If We willed, We could raise up a warner in every village

25:52.ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَجَٰهِدۡهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
25:52.en: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them herewith with a great endeavour

25:53.ar: ۞وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَرَجَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ هَٰذَا عَذۡبࣱ فُرَاتࣱ وَهَٰذَا مِلۡحٌ أُجَاجࣱ وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَهُمَا بَرۡزَخࣰ ا وَحِجۡرࣰ ا مَّحۡجُورࣰ ا
25:53.en: And He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and hath set a bar and a forbidding ban between them

25:54.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ بَشَرࣰ ا فَجَعَلَهُۥ نَسَبࣰ ا وَصِهۡرࣰ اۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرࣰ ا
25:54.en: And He it is Who hath created man from water, and hath appointed for him kindred by blood and kindred by marriage; for thy Lord is ever Powerful

25:55.ar: وَيَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُهُمۡ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمۡۗ وَكَانَ ٱلۡكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ ظَهِيرࣰ ا
25:55.en: Yet they worship instead of Allah that which can neither benefit them nor hurt them. The disbeliever was ever a partisan against his Lord

25:56.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
25:56.en: And We have sent thee (O Muhammad) only as a bearer of good tidings and a warner

25:57.ar: قُلۡ مَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:57.en: Say: I ask of you no reward for this, save that whoso will may choose a way unto his Lord

25:58.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱلۡحَيِّ ٱلَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِهِۦۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
25:58.en: And trust thou in the Living One Who dieth not, and hymn His praise. He sufficeth as the Knower of His bondmen's sins

25:59.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ فَسۡـَٔلۡ بِهِۦ خَبِيرࣰ ا
25:59.en: Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, then He mounted the Throne. The Beneficent! Ask anyone informed concerning Him

25:60.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسۡجُدُواْۤ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ قَالُواْ وَمَا ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ أَنَسۡجُدُ لِمَا تَأۡمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمۡ نُفُورࣰ ا۩
25:60.en: And when it is said unto them: Prostrate to the Beneficent! they say: And what is the Beneficent? Are we to prostrate to whatever thou (Muhammad) biddest us? And it increaseth aversion in them

25:61.ar: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَٰجࣰ ا وَقَمَرࣰ ا مُّنِيرࣰ ا
25:61.en: Blessed be He Who hath placed in the heaven mansions of the stars, and hath placed therein a great lamp and a moon giving light

26:2.en: These are revelations of the Scripture that maketh plain

26:3.ar: لَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعࣱ نَّفۡسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ
26:3.en: It may be that thou tormentest thyself (O Muhammad) because they believe not

26:4.ar: إِن نَّشَأۡ نُنَزِّلۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةࣰ فَظَلَّتۡ أَعۡنَٰقُهُمۡ لَهَا خَٰضِعِينَ
26:4.en: If We will, We can send down on them from the sky a portent so that their necks would remain bowed before it

26:5.ar: وَمَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن ذِكۡرࣲ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مُحۡدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُواْ عَنۡهُ مُعۡرِضِينَ
26:5.en: Never cometh there unto them a fresh reminder from the Beneficent One, but they turn away from it

26:6.ar: فَقَدۡ كَذَّبُواْ فَسَيَأۡتِيهِمۡ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُاْ مَا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
26:6.en: Now they have denied (the Truth); but there will come unto them tidings of that whereat they used to scoff

26:7.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمۡ أَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجࣲ كَرِيمٍ
26:7.en: Have they not seen the earth, how much of every fruitful kind We make to grow therein

26:8.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:8.en: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers

26:9.en: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:10.ar: وَإِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئۡتِ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
26:10.en: And when thy Lord called Moses, saying: Go unto the wrongdoing folk

26:11.en: The folk of Pharaoh. Will they not ward off (evil)

26:12.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
26:12.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I fear that they will deny me

26:13.ar: وَيَضِيقُ صَدۡرِي وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرۡسِلۡ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
26:13.en: And I shall be embarrassed, and my tongue will not speak plainly, therefor send for Aaron (to help me)

26:14.ar: وَلَهُمۡ عَلَيَّ ذَنۢبࣱ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقۡتُلُونِ
26:14.en: And they have a crime against me, so I fear that they will kill me

26:15.ar: قَالَ كَلَّاۖ فَٱذۡهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسۡتَمِعُونَ
26:15.en: He said: Nay, verily. So go ye twain with Our tokens. Lo! We shall be with you, Hearing

26:16.ar: فَأۡتِيَا فِرۡعَوۡنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:16.en: And come together unto Pharaoh and say: Lo! we bear a message of the Lord of the Worlds

26:17.en: (Saying): Let the Children of Israel go with us

26:18.ar: قَالَ أَلَمۡ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدࣰ ا وَلَبِثۡتَ فِينَا مِنۡ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
26:18.en: (Pharaoh) said (unto Moses): Did we not rear thee among us as a child? And thou didst dwell many years of thy life among us

26:19.ar: وَفَعَلۡتَ فَعۡلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلۡتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
26:19.en: And thou didst that thy deed which thou didst, and thou wast one of the ingrates

26:20.ar: قَالَ فَعَلۡتُهَآ إِذࣰ ا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
26:20.en: He said: I did it then, when I was of those who are astray

26:21.ar: فَفَرَرۡتُ مِنكُمۡ لَمَّا خِفۡتُكُمۡ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكۡمࣰ ا وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
26:21.en: Then I fled from you when I feared you, and my Lord vouchsafed me a command and appointed me (of the number) of those sent (by Him)

26:22.ar: وَتِلۡكَ نِعۡمَةࣱ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنۡ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
26:22.en: And this is the past favour wherewith thou reproachest me: that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel

26:23.en: Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the Worlds

26:24.ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
26:24.en: (Moses) said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye had but sure belief

26:25.en: (Pharaoh) said unto those around him: Hear ye not

26:26.en: He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers

26:27.ar: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُرۡسِلَ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمَجۡنُونࣱ‏
26:27.en: (Pharaoh) said: Lo! your messenger who hath been sent unto you is indeed a madman

26:28.ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآۖ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
26:28.en: He said: Lord of the East and the West and all that is between them, if ye did but understand

26:29.ar: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذۡتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيۡرِي لَأَجۡعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجُونِينَ
26:29.en: (Pharaoh) said: If thou choosest a god other than me, I assuredly shall place thee among the prisoners

26:30.en: He said: Even though I show thee something plain

26:31.ar: قَالَ فَأۡتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
26:31.en: (Pharaoh) said: Produce it then, if thou art of the truthful

26:32.ar: فَأَلۡقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعۡبَانࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
26:32.en: Then he flung down his staff and it became a serpent manifest

26:33.ar: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيۡضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
26:33.en: And he drew forth his hand and lo! it was white to the beholders

26:34.ar: قَالَ لِلۡمَلَإِ حَوۡلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
26:34.en: (Pharaoh) said unto the chiefs about him: Lo! this is verily a knowing wizard

26:35.ar: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنۡ أَرۡضِكُم بِسِحۡرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأۡمُرُونَ
26:35.en: Who would drive you out of your land by his magic. Now what counsel ye

26:36.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَرۡجِهۡ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبۡعَثۡ فِي ٱلۡمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
26:36.en: They said: Put him off, (him) and his brother, and send into the cities summoners

26:37.en: Who shall bring unto thee every knowing wizard

26:38.en: So the wizards were gathered together at a set time on a day appointed

26:39.en: And it was said unto the people: Are ye (also) gathering

26:40.ar: لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبِينَ
26:40.en: (They said): Aye, so that we may follow the wizards if they are the winners

26:41.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُواْ لِفِرۡعَوۡنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجۡرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبِينَ
26:41.en: And when the wizards came they said unto Pharaoh: Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners

26:42.ar: قَالَ نَعَمۡ وَإِنَّكُمۡ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلۡمُقَرَّبِينَ
26:42.en: He said: Aye, and ye will then surely be of those brought near (to me)

26:43.ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلۡقُواْ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلۡقُونَ
26:43.en: Moses said unto them: Throw what ye are going to throw

26:44.ar: فَأَلۡقَوۡاْ حِبَالَهُمۡ وَعِصِيَّهُمۡ وَقَالُواْ بِعِزَّةِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّا لَنَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبُونَ
26:44.en: Then they threw down their cords and their staves and said: By Pharaoh's might, lo! we verily are the winners

26:45.ar: فَأَلۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلۡقَفُ مَا يَأۡفِكُونَ
26:45.en: Then Moses threw his staff and lo! it swallowed that which they did falsely show

26:46.en: And the wizards were flung prostrate

26:47.en: Crying: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds

26:48.en: The Lord of Moses and Aaron

26:49.ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمۡ لَهُۥ قَبۡلَ أَنۡ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحۡرَ فَلَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَۚ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفࣲ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
26:49.en: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put your faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he doubtless is your chief who taught you magic! But verily ye shall come to know. Verily I will cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and verily I will crucify you every one

26:50.ar: قَالُواْ لَا ضَيۡرَۖ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
26:50.en: They said: It is no hurt, for lo! unto our Lord we shall return

26:51.ar: إِنَّا نَطۡمَعُ أَن يَغۡفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
26:51.en: Lo! we ardently hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we are the first of the believers

26:52.ar: ۞وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَسۡرِ بِعِبَادِيٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
26:52.en: And We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night, for ye will be pursued

26:53.en: Then Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners

26:54.en: (Who said): Lo! these indeed are but a little troop

26:55.en: And lo! they are offenders against us

26:56.en: And lo! we are a ready host

26:57.en: Thus did We take them away from gardens and watersprings

26:58.en: And treasures and a fair estate

26:59.en: Thus (were those things taken from them) and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them

26:60.en: And they overtook them at sunrise

26:61.ar: فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ قَالَ أَصۡحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدۡرَكُونَ
26:61.en: And when the two hosts saw each other, those with Moses said: Lo! we are indeed caught

25:63.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنࣰ ا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ ا
25:63.en: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace

25:64.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمۡ سُجَّدࣰ ا وَقِيَٰمࣰ ا
25:64.en: And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrate and standing

25:65.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصۡرِفۡ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَۖ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا
25:65.en: And who say: Our Lord! Avert from us the doom of hell; lo! the doom thereof is anguish

25:66.ar: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتۡ مُسۡتَقَرࣰّ ا وَمُقَامࣰ ا
25:66.en: Lo! it is wretched as abode and station

25:67.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمۡ يُسۡرِفُواْ وَلَمۡ يَقۡتُرُواْ وَكَانَ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامࣰ ا
25:67.en: And those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal nor grudging; and there is ever a firm station between the two

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

25:71.ar: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابࣰ ا
25:71.en: And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance

25:72.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشۡهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِٱللَّغۡوِ مَرُّواْ كِرَامࣰ ا
25:72.en: And those who will not witness vanity, but when they pass near senseless play, pass by with dignity

25:73.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ لَمۡ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيۡهَا صُمࣰّ ا وَعُمۡيَانࣰ ا
25:73.en: And those who, when they are reminded of the revelations of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat

25:74.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعۡيُنࣲ وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
25:74.en: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil)

25:75.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُجۡزَوۡنَ ٱلۡغُرۡفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيُلَقَّوۡنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةࣰ وَسَلَٰمًا
25:75.en: They will be awarded the high place forasmuch as they were steadfast, and they will meet therein with welcome and the ward of peace

25:76.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ حَسُنَتۡ مُسۡتَقَرࣰّ ا وَمُقَامࣰ ا
25:76.en: Abiding there for ever. Happy is it as abode and station

25:77.ar: قُلۡ مَا يَعۡبَؤُاْ بِكُمۡ رَبِّي لَوۡلَا دُعَآؤُكُمۡۖ فَقَدۡ كَذَّبۡتُمۡ فَسَوۡفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامَۢا
25:77.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): My Lord would not concern Himself with you but for your prayer. But now ye have denied (the Truth), therefor there will be judgment

26:62.ar: قَالَ كَلَّآۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهۡدِينِ
26:62.en: He said: Nay, verily! for lo! my Lord is with me. He will guide me

26:63.ar: فَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرۡقࣲ كَٱلطَّوۡدِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
26:63.en: Then We inspired Moses, saying: Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast

26:64.en: Then brought We near the others to that place

26:65.en: And We saved Moses and those with him, every one

26:67.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:67.en: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers

26:68.en: And lo, thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:69.en: Recite unto them the story of Abraham

26:70.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ
26:70.en: When he said unto his father and his folk: What worship ye

26:71.ar: قَالُواْ نَعۡبُدُ أَصۡنَامࣰ ا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
26:71.en: They said: We worship idols, and are ever devoted unto them

26:72.en: He said: Do they hear you when ye cry

26:73.en: Or do they benefit or harm you

26:74.ar: قَالُواْ بَلۡ وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفۡعَلُونَ
26:74.en: They said: Nay, but we found our fathers acting on this wise

26:75.en: He said: See now that which ye worship

26:77.ar: فَإِنَّهُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ لِّيٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:77.en: Lo! they are (all) an enemy unto me, save the Lord of the Worlds

26:78.en: Who created me, and He doth guide me

26:79.en: And Who feedeth me and watereth me

26:80.en: And when I sicken, then He healeth me

26:81.en: And Who causeth me to die, then giveth me life (again)

26:82.ar: وَٱلَّذِيٓ أَطۡمَعُ أَن يَغۡفِرَ لِي خَطِيٓـَٔتِي يَوۡمَ ٱلدِّينِ
26:82.en: And Who, I ardently hope, will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment

26:83.ar: رَبِّ هَبۡ لِي حُكۡمࣰ ا وَأَلۡحِقۡنِي بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
26:83.en: My Lord! Vouchsafe me wisdom and unite me to the righteous

26:84.ar: وَٱجۡعَل لِّي لِسَانَ صِدۡقࣲ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرِينَ
26:84.en: And give unto me a good report in later generations

26:85.en: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Delight

26:86.ar: وَٱغۡفِرۡ لِأَبِيٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
26:86.en: And forgive my father. Lo! he is of those who err

26:87.en: And abase me not on the day when they are raised

26:88.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالࣱ وَلَا بَنُونَ
26:88.en: The day when wealth and sons avail not (any man)

26:89.ar: إِلَّا مَنۡ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلۡبࣲ سَلِيمࣲ‏
26:89.en: Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart

26:105.en: Noah's folk denied the messengers (of Allah)

26:106.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ أَخُوهُمۡ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
26:106.en: When their brother Noah said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil)

26:107.en: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

26:108.en: So keep your duty to Allah, and obey me

26:109.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:109.en: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds

26:110.en: So keep your duty to Allah, and obey me

26:111.en: They said: Shall we put faith in thee, when the lowest (of the people) follow thee

26:112.ar: قَالَ وَمَا عِلۡمِي بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
26:112.en: He said: And what knowledge have I of what they may have been doing (in the past)

26:113.ar: إِنۡ حِسَابُهُمۡ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّيۖ لَوۡ تَشۡعُرُونَ
26:113.en: Lo! their reckoning is my Lord's concern, if ye but knew

26:114.en: And I am not (here) to repulse believers

26:115.en: I am only a plain warner

26:116.ar: قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَرۡجُومِينَ
26:116.en: They said: If thou cease not, O Noah, thou wilt surely be among those stoned (to death)

26:117.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! my own folk deny me

26:118.ar: فَٱفۡتَحۡ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَهُمۡ فَتۡحࣰ ا وَنَجِّنِي وَمَن مَّعِيَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
26:118.en: Therefor judge Thou between us, a (conclusive) judgment, and save me and those believers who are with me

26:119.ar: فَأَنجَيۡنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلۡمَشۡحُونِ
26:119.en: And We saved him and those with him in the laden ship

26:120.en: Then afterward We drowned the others

26:121.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:121.en: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers

26:122.en: And lo, thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:123.en: (The tribe of) A'ad denied the messengers (of Allah)

26:124.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ أَخُوهُمۡ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
26:124.en: When their brother Hud said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil)

26:125.en: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

26:126.en: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me

26:127.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:127.en: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds

26:128.en: Build ye on every high place a monument for vain delight

26:129.en: And seek ye out strongholds, that haply ye may last for ever

26:130.en: And if ye seize by force, seize ye as tyrants

26:131.en: Rather keep your duty to Allah, and obey me

26:132.en: Keep your duty toward Him Who hath aided you with (the good things) that ye know

26:133.en: Hath aided you with cattle and sons

26:135.ar: إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
26:135.en: Lo! I fear for you the retribution of an awful day

26:136.ar: قَالُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡنَآ أَوَعَظۡتَ أَمۡ لَمۡ تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡوَٰعِظِينَ
26:136.en: They said: It is all one to us whether thou preachest or art not of those who preach

26:137.en: This is but a fable of the men of old

26:138.en: And we shall not be doomed

26:139.ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَهۡلَكۡنَٰهُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:139.en: And they denied him; therefor We destroyed them. Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers

26:140.en: And lo! thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:141.en: (The tribe of) Thamud denied the messengers (of Allah)

26:142.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ أَخُوهُمۡ صَٰلِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
26:142.en: When their brother Salih said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil)

26:143.en: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

26:144.en: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me

26:145.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:145.en: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds

26:146.en: Will ye be left secure in that which is here before us

26:148.en: And tilled fields and heavy-sheathed palm-trees

26:149.ar: وَتَنۡحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ بُيُوتࣰ ا فَٰرِهِينَ
26:149.en: Though ye hew out dwellings in the mountain, being skilful

26:150.en: Therefor keep your duty to Allah and obey me

26:151.en: And obey not the command of the prodigal

26:152.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا يُصۡلِحُونَ
26:152.en: Who spread corruption in the earth, and reform not

26:153.en: They said: Thou art but one of the bewitched

26:154.ar: مَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا فَأۡتِ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
26:154.en: Thou art but a mortal like us. So bring some token if thou art of the truthful

26:155.ar: قَالَ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةࣱ لَّهَا شِرۡبࣱ وَلَكُمۡ شِرۡبُ يَوۡمࣲ مَّعۡلُومࣲ‏
26:155.en: He said: (Behold) this she-camel. She hath the right to drink (at the well), and ye have the right to drink, (each) on an appointed day

26:156.ar: وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءࣲ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابُ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
26:156.en: And touch her not with ill lest there come on you the retribution of an awful day

26:157.en: But they hamstrung her, and then were penitent

26:158.ar: فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:158.en: So the retribution came on them. Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers

26:159.en: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:160.en: The folk of Lot denied the messengers (of Allah)

26:161.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ أَخُوهُمۡ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
26:161.en: When their brother Lot said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil)

26:162.en: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

26:163.en: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me

26:164.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:164.en: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds

26:165.en: What! Of all creatures do ye come unto the males

26:166.ar: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمٌ عَادُونَ
26:166.en: And leave the wives your Lord created for you? Nay, but ye are froward folk

26:167.ar: قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُخۡرَجِينَ
26:167.en: They said: If thou cease not, O Lot, thou wilt soon be of the outcast

26:168.en: He said: I am in truth of those who hate your conduct

26:169.en: My Lord! Save me and my household from what they do

26:170.en: So We saved him and his household, every one

26:171.en: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind

26:172.en: Then afterward We destroyed the others

26:173.ar: وَأَمۡطَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم مَّطَرࣰ اۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلۡمُنذَرِينَ
26:173.en: And We rained on them a rain. And dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned

26:174.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:174.en: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers

26:175.en: And lo! thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

26:176.en: The dwellers in the wood (of Midian) denied the messengers (of Allah)

26:177.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ شُعَيۡبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
26:177.en: When Shu'eyb said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil)

26:178.en: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

26:179.en: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me

26:180.ar: وَمَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:180.en: And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds

26:181.en: Give full measure, and be not of those who give less (than the due)

26:182.en: And weigh with the true balance

26:183.ar: وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡثَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُفۡسِدِينَ
26:183.en: Wrong not mankind in their goods, and do not evil, making mischief, in the earth

26:184.en: And keep your duty unto Him Who created you and the generations of the men of old

26:185.en: They said: Thou art but one of the bewitched

26:186.ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
26:186.en: Thou art but a mortal like us, and lo! we deem thee of the liars

26:187.ar: فَأَسۡقِطۡ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
26:187.en: Then make fragments of the heaven fall upon us, if thou art of the truthful

26:188.en: He said: My Lord is Best Aware of what ye do

26:189.ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمۡ عَذَابُ يَوۡمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمٍ
26:189.en: But they denied him, so there came on them the retribution of the day of gloom. Lo! it was the retribution of an awful day

26:190.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
26:190.en: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers

26:191.en: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful

om7wGc-ctmk.speaker: adnan
om7wGc-ctmk.title: A Juz A Day, Juz 19: Is There a God Besides Allah?
om7wGc-ctmk.one_line: Al-Furqan and Ash-Shuara: the objections to the Quran, the traits of the servants of the Most Compassionate, and the one message all prophets carried.
om7wGc-ctmk.summary: He reads Al-Furqan as a set of claims against the Prophet and the Quran with Allah's replies: they call it fables, mock a messenger who eats and walks the markets, and demand physical miracles, when the real issue is that they deny the Hour. He points out that attacking the person instead of the content derails any argument, and that people themselves are often a test for one another, as with the friend who leads someone away from the Messenger and leaves him biting his hands in regret. He laments the Prophet's complaint that his people neglected the Quran, calls the Quran itself the great jihad of ideas, and presents the servants of the Most Compassionate as Allah's answer to those who asked who He is: believers whose humility, night prayer, moderation, repentance and dignity are themselves a sign and a form of dawah. Ash-Shuara then shows Musa outmanoeuvring Pharaoh's smears, the magicians' instant faith, Ibrahim's refusal to attribute illness to Allah, and the identical words of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shuayb, revealing a single core message. He asks listeners to understand and live the Quran, make heartfelt dua in their own language, and recite Ibrahim's dua.

outline.heading: Opening
What belongs to Allah alone
outline.gist: He sent the Criterion, owns the heavens and earth, has no child or partner and ordained everything precisely, while idols create nothing and control nothing.

outline.heading: Their claims: fabricated fables and an ordinary messenger
outline.gist: They say the Quran is borrowed fables and ask why a messenger eats and works, or why no angel or treasure came with him.

outline.heading: Attacking the person instead of the content
outline.gist: Calling him bewitched is character assassination; whoever attacks the speaker rather than the argument loses the point entirely.

outline.heading: Physical miracles do not convince
outline.gist: Those who demand signs would not believe them; those seeking truth find the message and creation miraculous enough. The real issue is denial of the Hour.

outline.heading: The fire that growls from afar
outline.gist: Chained in a narrow place, they beg for annihilation; the descriptions are meant to stop us in our tracks.

outline.heading: The garden of eternity: whatever they wish, forever
outline.gist: Paradise in one sentence, a promise binding on Allah.

outline.heading: The worshipped disown their worshippers
outline.gist: Righteous figures people worshipped deny ever claiming it; long enjoyment made them complacent until they forgot the reminder.

outline.heading: Every messenger ate food and walked the markets
outline.gist: All prophets were humans who worked like everyone else.

outline.heading: People made a test for one another
outline.gist: Difficult people in our lives test our patience; address the problem without attacking the person.

outline.heading: The heavens burst and angels descend
outline.gist: On that day true authority belongs only to the Most Compassionate.

outline.heading: Biting his hands: the friend who led me astray
outline.gist: Someone who had guidance laments taking a friend who pulled him from the Messenger's way, an example of people as trials.

outline.heading: The Prophet's complaint: they neglected this Quran
outline.gist: Memorisation and recitation are common, but understanding and implementation are far rarer.

outline.heading: Revealed in stages to steady the heart
outline.gist: Gradual revelation reassured the Prophet, and reading it steadily through life strengthens the believer's heart.

outline.heading: Peoples of the past each given lessons, then destroyed
outline.gist: Musa and Harun, Nuh, Ad, Thamud and the people of the well all rejected clear lessons.

outline.heading: Taking one's desires as a god
outline.gist: Self-centred pursuit of pleasure turns the self into a god, a danger in a materialistic society.

outline.heading: Shade, night and sleep: thriving within Allah's system
outline.gist: We thrive when we live by the rhythm He created, and the same holds for living by His law.

outline.heading: Winds bearing mercy and pure rain
outline.gist: Rain revives barren land and starts the cycle of life for animals and people.

outline.heading: The same idea in many forms
outline.gist: The Quran repeats core examples and the six core prophets layer by layer, like a remix, so the message is fully grasped.

outline.heading: Ingratitude as burying the longing for one's Lord
outline.gist: Kufr here is persisting in desire and materialism without asking whether life has a bigger purpose.

outline.heading: Strive against them with the Quran: the great jihad
outline.gist: The Quran's arguments are how we wage the ongoing war of ideas, though the ummah's weakness has diminished our ability to convey it.

outline.heading: Two seas, a humble fluid, and bonds of kinship
outline.gist: The barrier between waters and the improbable creation of each human show His power, yet people worship what cannot help them.

outline.heading: No payment asked; trust the Ever-Living
outline.gist: The Prophet seeks no money; reliance on Allah and glorifying Him is how one stays patient and resilient.

outline.heading: Who is the Most Compassionate?
outline.gist: Quraysh mocked the name; rather than argue semantics, Allah answers by describing His servants.

outline.heading: The servants of the Most Compassionate: humility, peace, night prayer, moderation
outline.gist: Their conduct is itself a sign of Allah and the truest dawah: they walk humbly, answer provocation with peace and spend in balance.

outline.heading: Dua to Allah alone; sanctity of life and chastity
outline.gist: They call on no one but Allah, take no life except through lawful process and avoid fornication.

outline.heading: Evil deeds turned into good
outline.gist: Those who repent are not only forgiven; Allah converts even major sins into good deeds.

outline.heading: No false witness; a prayer for spouses and children
outline.gist: They pass by falsehood with dignity, heed reminders and ask for families that are the joy of their eyes, earning lofty mansions.

outline.heading: What are you to my Lord without your supplication?
outline.gist: Dua is what connects us to Allah; anyone struggling with the commands should start with heartfelt dua in their own language.

outline.heading: Ash-Shuara: the Almighty, the Most Merciful
outline.gist: A refrain that frames each prophet's story in the surah.

outline.heading: Grieving over their disbelief; no compelling sign
outline.gist: Used to being believed for forty years, the Prophet was pained by rejection; Allah leaves people free to choose and points them to the plants of the earth.

outline.heading: Musa's fears and his commission
outline.gist: He fears rejection, a tied tongue and a murder charge; Allah assures him and sends him with Harun to demand freedom for the Israelites.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's smear and Musa's retort
outline.gist: Pharaoh paints him as ungrateful and dangerous, as powers make the oppressed look like oppressors; Musa asks how raising him can be a favour when his whole people are enslaved.

outline.heading: Lord of the heavens, the east and the west
outline.gist: Musa keeps returning to Allah until Pharaoh loses the argument and, like failing empires, turns to threats.

outline.heading: The staff, the shining hand, and a national security threat
outline.gist: Pharaoh frames Musa as a magician out to expel them and summons sorcerers.

outline.heading: The magicians prostrate
outline.gist: Hired for a fee, they see a true sign and believe at once, unmoved by threats of mutilation and crucifixion.

outline.heading: The exodus and the armies face to face
outline.gist: Pharaoh dismisses the fleeing Israelites as a handful; at the sea his people cry that they are caught.

outline.heading: My Lord is with me: the sea parts
outline.gist: Musa's certainty answers his people's panic; the deliverance shows Allah's mercy and the tyrant's end His might.

outline.heading: Ibrahim questions the idols
outline.gist: Can they hear, help or harm? Their only answer is culture and their forefathers.

outline.heading: When I am sick, He heals me
outline.gist: Ibrahim credits Allah with every good and does not attribute illness to Him, an expression of true faith and patience.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's dua and the pure heart
outline.gist: He asks for wisdom, the company of the righteous, good mention and forgiveness for his father; only a sound heart will save, and the dua is one to recite in the last nights.

outline.heading: Nuh: fear Allah, obey me, I ask no reward
outline.gist: The first of several prophets whose words are given in identical form.

outline.heading: Hud repeats the same message
outline.gist: The same call, the same rejection, the same refrain.

outline.heading: Salih and the she-camel
outline.gist: A physical sign was given, yet they killed the camel and were destroyed.

outline.heading: Lut, and why every prophet speaks the same words
outline.gist: All messengers shared one core message of taqwa, obedience and no material motive, then addressed their people's specific problems.

outline.heading: Shuayb and the people of the forest: why not their brother
outline.gist: They worshipped the forest, so Shuayb is not called their brother; kinship in land and humanity does not extend into false worship.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The Quran
themes.note: Objections to the Quran and their answers, the Prophet's complaint that it was neglected, and its gradual revelation.

themes.label: The Quran
themes.note: The Quran as the great jihad of ideas that Muslims must understand and convey.

themes.label: Character of the servants of the Most Compassionate
themes.note: Humility, peaceful replies, night prayer, moderate spending and dignity make believers a living sign of Allah.

themes.label: Prophets
themes.note: Musa against Pharaoh, Ibrahim against idols, and the identical core message of five prophets.

themes.label: The Hereafter
themes.note: Scenes of the fire, the garden of eternity and the regret of those misled by friends.

themes.label: People as trials
themes.note: People are tests for one another; respond with patience and do not attack the person.

themes.label: Dua
themes.note: Supplication is what connects us to Allah and is the place to begin.

themes.label: Dua

themes.label: Tawhid
themes.note: What is exclusive to Allah, against idols that control nothing.

themes.label: Narrative and smear

maxims: Attack the content, not the person
People are made tests for one another
The Quran is the great jihad
The servants of the Most Compassionate are a sign of Allah
Everything else is a misdirection

stories.point: Musa refuses to be distracted by smears and keeps the conversation on Allah until Pharaoh resorts to threats.
Those who came to defeat the prophet became his best followers once they saw the truth and had the humility to accept it.
Logic against inherited idol worship, and still a dua for his father's forgiveness.

stories.who: A young hafiz's calligraphy gift to his father
stories.point: A light-hearted contrast to Ibrahim's sincere prayer for his father.

contemporary: Materialistic modern society that turns desires into a god
World powers that portray the oppressed as the oppressors
Empires that resort to bombing when they run out of arguments
The ummah's weakness in conveying the Quran in today's war of ideas
takeaways: In disagreements, address the content and not the person
Move from reciting the Quran to understanding and acting on it
